chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.

15.original: [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.]
15.content: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Two Trees (Kephalaia Core Layer)

---

**¶12:** [GAP-1] The interior knowledges that clothe the external form of [GAP-2] this perception rooted in divine wisdom. They are the scattered elements of wisdom that have been dispersed and intermingled, compounded throughout the whole natural mind.

**¶15:** This perception possesses five distinct faculties of spiritual life. [GAP-3: REVIEW They are the outermost reception, the sustaining guidance, the interior seeing, the active understanding, and the inmost willing.] The outermost reception is the communion of those conjoined in charity. [GAP-4: REVIEW The sustaining guidance] is the supporting column of divine truth, which is the Divine Human Form. [The interior seeing is the pri]mordial divine wisdom that dwells within the doctrine of living truth. The active understanding is the mediating divine love [GAP-5: REVIEW that dwells within] the doctrine of celestial love, which radiates into [GAP-6] all surrounding states. Also, the inmost willing is the Divine Itself dwelling in supreme perfection, complete within the heavenly degrees of wisdom.

**¶17:** It is the outermost reception that shall [GAP-7] begin the elevation, and they shall be raised up [GAP-8] through the sustaining guidance; they shall be raised up to interior seeing, which is the primordial divine wisdom dwelling within the doctrine that carries truth through states of obscurity; from interior seeing they shall rise up to active understanding, which is the mediating divine love dwelling within the doctrine that carries truth through states of illumination. And this great and glorious active understanding shall bring them inward to the inmost willing — which is the Divine Itself, the God of truth, the supreme Wisdom of all the heavenly degrees of glory.

**¶19:** [GAP-9] the perverted [GAP-10] arises in [GAP-11] from [GAP-12] also [GAP-13] the manner in which it is [GAP-14] the perception rooted in divine wisdom [GAP-15] of love turned inward [GAP-16] they are the dominant compulsions [GAP-17] the internal state and the recurring cycle of natural life [GAP-18] they are the five forms of the proprium that move through the world [GAP-19] works [GAP-20] instruction proceeding from falsity, the hidden principle that [GAP-21] the ruling evil implanted in the external mind.

**¶22:** The perception rooted in self-intelligence has five faculties. They are reception, guidance, seeing, understanding, and willing — but inverted. Its reception is the governing principle of spiritual death. Its guidance is the endless revolving [GAP-22] from one false appearance into another. Also, its seeing is the consuming fire of self-love [GAP-23] the inner torment, which is filled with dense falsity. Its understanding [GAP-24] is a containing form emptied of life. Its willing is the [GAP-25] ultimate mass of consolidated evil, the final bondage, the [GAP-26], those states that the ruling evil cast out [GAP-27] the great [GAP-28] and they descend [GAP-29] into falsity from evil [GAP-30] all [GAP-31] and they strip away [GAP-32] are consumed into that ultimate mass of consolidated evil, and they are held captive [GAP-33] the works of falsity from evil, the same that they [GAP-34] to perpetuity without end [GAP-35] his perception [GAP-36] shall arrive at that state; and within it there is no turning back.

**¶24:** [GAP-37] which lies within the natural mind receptive to the Divine [GAP-38] spiritual life and wisdom; since spiritual death and falsity from evil do not exist there [GAP-39]. Also, the perception rooted in self-intelligence is the unregenerate proprium [GAP-40] which occurs within the natural mind receptive only to evil [GAP-41] falsity and spiritual death.

**¶25:** One understands that these two perceptions did not arise out of one another, nor did they proceed from one another. They did not come from a single origin! The person who can distinguish and separate them may ascend into the heavenly state of wisdom.

**¶26:** Works of evil did not arise from the perception rooted in wisdom [GAP-42]; but whoever will not distinguish [GAP-43] the one from the other falls into the state of falsity from evil [GAP-44] until he arrives at the [GAP-45] final state from which there is no return.

---

### Translator's Note

The entire chapter teaches that the regenerating mind and the unregenerate mind each possess five ascending degrees — identical in structure but opposite in quality. In the perception rooted in wisdom, these degrees form a ladder of ascent from the outermost communion of charity inward to the Divine Itself. In the perception rooted in self-intelligence, the same five degrees form a descending spiral: from the rule of spiritual death, through endless falsification, through the consuming fire of self-love, through empty forms devoid of life, into a final consolidated mass of evil from which no liberation is possible. The teaching's core spiritual imperative (¶25–26) is *discrimination*: the ability to separate what is of wisdom from what is of self-intelligence constitutes the very act of regeneration, and the failure to discriminate constitutes spiritual death.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [These are] the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [of] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.

it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] Its consideration is the holy church. [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [the world] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.

It is consideration that shall [receive them, and] they shall be raised up [to what] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.

[Also, the] bad [things that] happen in [the world] from [the bad tree] also [in] the way that it is [with] the good tree [so also the tree] of the fire [Also] they are the ruling-power [of] heaven and the wheel [Also] they are the five fleshes that walk [in the world. Their] fruit [is the te]aching as of error, the mystery that [was hidden, wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.

The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death. Its counsel is transmigration [of the soul] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [and the ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [is the dark] vessel. Its mind is the [pit] the lump, the last bond, the [stone], they that Satan cast away [into] the great [fire] and they fall [into] the Darkness [and] all [ ... ] and they take away [ ... ] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [in] the fruit of Darkness, the one that they [shall bear] for ever and ever [ ... ] his face [ ... ] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.

[The good tree is the Light] which lies in its good earth [full of life] and light; as death and Darkness do not exist [in it] Also, the bad tree is Matter [and Darkness wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [full of] Darkness and death.
He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light
bad fruit did not arise from it [at any time]; but whoever will not separate out [the one] from one another, he falls to the land of Darkness [ ... ] until he arrives at the [lump]

fills.explanation: The identification pattern "These are... They are..." is standard in the Kephalaia's expository register, and the spiritual reading confirms an identification of the intellectuals as interior knowledges clothing the good tree.
The spiritual reading maps this to "the external form of this perception rooted in divine wisdom," requiring the genitive connector "of" to link "its body" to "this good tree."

fills.fill: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.
fills.original: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.
fills.explanation: The editor's fill is confirmed by the identical five-faculty list appearing later in ¶22 ("They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind") and by the individual identifications that immediately follow in ¶15.

The editor's fill is confirmed by the sequential pattern identifying each limb: "Its consideration is... Its counsel is... Its insight is... Its thought is... the mind is..." which runs through the entire paragraph.
The editor's fill is confirmed by the repeated formula "who dwells in the ship of..." used for the First Man and the Father throughout this passage.

The Third Ambassador dwells in the ship of living fire (the sun in Manichaean cosmology), which shines upon the world; the spiritual reading's "all surrounding states" corresponds to the visible world illuminated by the sun's radiance.
Consideration is identified as the holy church (outermost reception in the spiritual reading), so it receives the ascending souls first, beginning the process of elevation through the five degrees.

The ascending pattern throughout ¶17 uses "raised up to" each successive faculty; "to what is counsel" parallels "to insight, which is the First Man" and provides the identification of the second degree.

The Kephalaia consistently uses "Also" to transition between parallel discussions; ¶19 shifts from the good tree (¶15–17) to the bad tree, requiring the standard transitional "Also, the" before "bad."

The sentence structure requires a noun and relative pronoun between "bad" and "happen" to form the subject: "the bad things that happen in the world," corresponding to the spiritual reading's "the perverted arises in."
In the Kephalaia, evil manifestations occur "in the world"; the spiritual reading's "arises in [GAP-11]" requires a locus, and the world is the natural-plane setting for the bad tree's operations.

The passage identifies the source of bad things in the world; "from the bad tree" names this source directly, paralleling the good tree mentioned immediately after, and anticipating its further identification as "the tree of the fire" at GAP-15.
The preposition "in" naturally connects "also" to "the way that it is with the good tree," forming the comparison "also in the way that it is with the good tree."
The passage compares the bad tree's structure to the good tree; "the way that it is with the good tree" is standard comparative construction in the Kephalaia's register.

The passage compares the two trees; "the way that it is with the good tree, so also the tree of the fire" is a standard Kephalaia comparative construction transitioning from the good tree to the bad tree (tree of fire/desire).

The Kephalaia consistently uses "Also" to introduce each successive attribute in a list; here it transitions from naming the tree of fire to its first worldly manifestation, parallel to GAP-18's identical transition to the next attribute.
The genitive "of" connects "ruling-power" to "heaven and the wheel," identifying the dominant compulsions as the ruling-power of heaven (the firmament) and the wheel (the zodiac/cycle of rebirth).

The transition between two parallel "they are..." descriptions of the bad tree's manifestations follows the Kephalaia's standard "Also" connector for listing successive attributes of a single subject.
The five fleshes walk "in the world" (the spiritual reading's "move through the world"), and "Their" introduces the possessive connecting to "fruit" as the works/fruit of the five fleshes.
Completing the identification "fruit is the teaching as of error," where "te" + "aching" forms "teaching"; the spiritual reading identifies this as instruction proceeding from falsity.

"The mystery that was hidden" is a well-attested gnostic-Manichaean formula; "wh" + "ich" completes "which," yielding "the mystery that was hidden, which Satan appointed in the world," matching the spiritual reading's "hidden principle."

In Manichaean doctrine, transmigration specifically denotes the soul's passage through successive bodily forms; "transmigration of the soul in type after type" is standard terminology for the endless revolving through false appearances.

The conjunction "and" links "furnaces of fire" to "gehenna" as two aspects of the same degree of punishment; "ge" + "henna" completes "gehenna," which the spiritual reading identifies as inner torment.

The bad tree's thought is a dark vessel, directly contrasting the good tree's thought which is the Ambassador dwelling in the ship of living fire; the spiritual reading describes it as a containing form emptied of life, hence "dark."

In standard Manichaean eschatological terminology, the pit (bothros) is listed alongside the lump (bolos) and the stone (lithos) as components of the final sealing of evil; the pit is the first item in this list.

The stone (lithos) is the traditional fourth element of the Manichaean eschatological sealing, following the pit, the lump, and the bond; it represents the covering that permanently seals evil in the pit.
The directional preposition "into" connects "cast away" to "the great fire," indicating Satan cast the evil states downward into the great fire of final punishment.
"The great fire" is standard Manichaean eschatological language for the final conflagration; it naturally precedes "and they fall into the Darkness" as the sequence of descending punishments.
The directional preposition "into" is required by the verb "fall" and the destination "the Darkness," forming "they fall into the Darkness" as a standard expression of descent into evil.

The paratactic chain "and they fall into the Darkness, and all... and they take away... are swallowed into the lump" requires the conjunction "and" to maintain the characteristic Coptic prose style linking successive actions in the eschatological descent.

The preposition "in" connects "bound" to "the fruit of Darkness," indicating captivity within the consolidated works of evil; the spiritual reading confirms they are "held captive" within these works.

"The fruit of Darkness, the one that they shall bear for ever" expresses the perpetual burden of evil's consequences; "bear" connects to "fruit" both as carrying and as producing, matching the spiritual reading's "to perpetuity without end."

fills.fill: The good tree is the Light
fills.explanation: The direct parallel with "the bad tree is Matter" requires the good tree to be identified with its ontological principle; in Manichaean cosmology, the good tree = the Light, just as the bad tree = Matter/Darkness.

The good earth is characterized by life and light (paralleling the bad earth's Darkness and death); "full of life and light" completes the description, with "life" matching the partial word visible in the manuscript.
The locative phrase "in it" completes the clause "death and Darkness do not exist in it," referring back to the good earth; the spiritual reading confirms "do not exist there."

Paralleling the good tree's identification as "the Light," the bad tree is "Matter and Darkness"; "wh" + "ich" completes "which," giving "the bad tree is Matter and Darkness which occurs in its bad earth."
Directly paralleling the good earth's description "full of life and light," the bad earth is "full of Darkness and death," completing the antithetical structure of ¶24.
The temporal phrase emphasizes that bad fruit never arose from the good tree, reinforcing the absolute separation of the two principles that is the chapter's central teaching.

The spiritual reading specifies "distinguish the one from the other," and "the one" is the object that must be separated out "from one another," directly paralleling the discrimination imperative of ¶25.

The lump (bolos) is the final consolidated mass of evil described in ¶22 as the mind of the bad tree; the spiritual reading's "final state from which there is no return" identifies this as the eschatological endpoint for those who fail to discriminate.
